interactions.teaches: Selecting H, HO, or CO2H shows that each substituent on one stereocenter has an identical reflected partner on the other stereocenter across the internal plane

interactions.label: Guided focus
interactions.teaches: Stepping through the matched pairs builds the meso argument: the upper and lower halves are related by reflection, so the molecule is achiral despite two chirality centers
Rotating the ball-and-stick model reveals that the cyan sheet is a real internal mirror plane in three dimensions, not merely a horizontal line in the drawing

demo_steps.title: Side-by-side comparison
demo_steps.narration: Both representations are visible at once, matching the source figure: the flat stereochemical drawing is on the left and the 3D ball-and-stick model is on the right. The same pale cyan plane cuts between the two carbon centers in both views.

demo_steps.title: Check the hydrogens
demo_steps.narration: The upper H and lower H lie on opposite sides of the same horizontal plane. They are mirror partners, so selecting one should mark only the corresponding H on the other half.

demo_steps.title: Check the hydroxyl groups
demo_steps.narration: The two HO groups occupy reflected positions on the left side of the molecule. The structural wedges and the 3D red oxygen groups show the same upper-to-lower reflection.

demo_steps.title: Check the carboxyl groups
demo_steps.narration: The CO2H groups on the right are also related by reflection through the plane. Matching all substituent types confirms that one half of the molecule mirrors the other.

demo_steps.title: Meso conclusion
demo_steps.narration: All three substituent pairs match across the plane. Because the molecule contains an internal symmetry plane, it is superimposable on its mirror image and is meso rather than optically active.

plan.geometry_notes: Overall layout: use a wide frame about 7.2 world units wide by 3.4 high. Default view MUST show both panels simultaneously, with no representation toggle. Place the structural drawing on the left centered at x=-2.25, y=0, z=0, scaled to about 2.15 units tall and 1.9 units wide. Place the ball-and-stick model on the right centered at x=2.15, y=0, z=0, about 2.7 units tall and 2.4 units wide. Leave about 0.7 world units of empty space between the structural formula and molecular model so they read as paired but separate depictions. Color palette: black bonds/text #111111, structural H blue #0076b6, structural HO magenta #d61aa0, structural CO2H green #15894f, central carbon dark gray #4f5b5f, model bonds light gray #b8b8b8, oxygen red #c33a2f, hydrogen blue #2d8fd7, carboxyl-group green #22a86b, symmetry plane pale cyan #bdefff with opacity 0.38 to 0.48, selection halo yellow #ffd54a with low opacity. Structural drawing coordinates are local to the left panel before applying the x=-2.25 offset: upper C text at (0, 0.58, 0), lower C text at (0, -0.58, 0), vertical C-C bond from (0, 0.42, 0) to (0, -0.42, 0). Upper H at (0, 1.18, 0) with a dashed vertical bond from (0, 0.72, 0) to (0, 1.02, 0). Lower H at (0, -1.18, 0) with a dashed vertical bond from (0, -0.72, 0) to (0, -1.02, 0). Upper HO label at (-0.73, 0.82, 0), connected to upper C by a filled triangular wedge whose narrow point touches the C and whose wide end points upper-left. Lower HO label at (-0.73, -0.82, 0), connected by the vertically mirrored wedge. Upper CO2H label at (0.88, 0.82, 0), connected by a simple solid slanted bond from the upper C toward upper-right. Lower CO2H label at (0.88, -0.82, 0), connected by the vertically mirrored solid slanted bond. Use CO₂H with subscript 2 if possible. Structural symmetry plane: draw a thin translucent parallelogram centered at local (0, 0, -0.025), long horizontal dimension about 1.65 units, apparent thickness/depth about 0.38 units, with the left and right edges slanting slightly down-left/up-right so it reads like the pale blue edge-on plane in the source. Put the label 'Symmetry plane' in black at local (1.25, -0.06, 0.02), aligned horizontally. Molecular model coordinates are local to the right panel before applying the x=2.15 offset. Use +Y as vertical screen direction; the mirror plane is the horizontal XZ plane at y=0. Set upper central carbon at (0, 0.62, 0), lower central carbon at (0, -0.62, 0), radius 0.19, joined by a cylinder radius 0.055. Use genuinely tetrahedral-looking substituent directions: the C-C bond from the upper carbon points downward toward the lower carbon, while the three upper substituent bonds point generally upward with separated x/z depth components; the lower half is the exact reflection across y=0, so x and z coordinates are identical and y coordinates change sign. Upper H sphere radius 0.105 at (0.05, 0.86, -0.62), connected to upper carbon; lower H at (0.05, -0.86, -0.62). Upper HO first red oxygen radius 0.16 at (-0.58, 0.86, 0.38), connected to upper carbon; upper second small red sphere radius 0.105 at (-0.82, 1.20, 0.62), connected to the first red oxygen. Lower HO first red oxygen at (-0.58, -0.86, 0.38), lower second red sphere at (-0.82, -1.20, 0.62). Upper CO2H main green sphere radius 0.18 at (0.62, 0.86, 0.12), connected to upper carbon; upper branch green sphere radius 0.155 at (0.82, 1.30, -0.18), upper small terminal green sphere radius 0.105 at (1.08, 1.54, -0.35), and upper right terminal green sphere radius 0.14 at (1.13, 0.83, 0.22). Lower CO2H main green sphere at (0.62, -0.86, 0.12), lower branch green sphere at (0.82, -1.30, -0.18), lower small terminal green sphere at (1.08, -1.54, -0.35), and lower right terminal green sphere at (1.13, -0.83, 0.22). Add cylinders between each bonded pair. Molecular symmetry plane: translucent pale cyan rectangle/parallelogram lying exactly in y=0, centered near local (0.18, 0, 0), spanning x from about -1.25 to +1.45 and z from -0.58 to +0.72; orient it so the front edge appears nearly horizontal and the receding edges show slight perspective. It must pass between, not through, the two central carbon spheres. Equal substituent types must have equal sizes in the upper and lower halves. Selection halos: hidden when guidedFocus='none' and when no click target is selected. When active, use thin low-opacity yellow outline rings or small glow shells around only the selected group and its mirror partner; do not show large default yellow rings and do not obscure the cyan plane.
plan.notes: Render the scene as a simultaneous comparison, not as separate panels hidden behind a representation toggle. Keep the structural drawing fixed in screen-facing orientation on the left while allowing orbit interaction to rotate only the right molecular-model group or a right-side orbit container; the left drawing should not spin away from the reader. Use CSS2D or signed-distance-field text for crisp C, H, HO, CO₂H, and Symmetry plane labels. Use triangular meshes for wedge bonds and segmented line geometry for dashed bonds. For the molecule, use MeshStandardMaterial with clear directional lighting and ambient fill; enable depth testing so front and back substituents occlude correctly. Use transparent material for cyan planes with depthWrite=false and renderOrder after opaque atoms so the plane remains visible without hiding the model. Click targets should be group-level: H, HO, and CO2H on either the structural drawing or the molecule; clicking an upper group highlights the lower mirror partner and clicking a lower group highlights the upper mirror partner. The guidedFocus state should drive the same subtle highlight system used by clicks, with 'none' showing no halos.

authoredPrompt: This figure pairs a flat structural drawing with a three-dimensional model of the same molecule, both cut by a horizontal plane. On the left, two carbons lettered "C" sit one above the other, joined by a vertical bond. The upper carbon bears an "H" above it on a dashed bond, an "HO" group at the left in magenta on a bold wedge, and a "CO2H" group at the right in green. The lower carbon repeats that arrangement flipped vertically: "HO" again at the left and "CO2H" at the right, but its "H" now points downward on a dashed bond. A pale blue parallelogram drawn edge-on slices horizontally between the two carbons, labeled "Symmetry plane". On the right the molecule appears as a ball-and-stick model, two dark gray carbons stacked vertically, each carrying a small blue sphere, a red oxygen with a second red sphere beyond it, and a branching green group, with an identical pale blue plane passing between them. Running the plane through both depictions asks the reader to check one half against the other. Because the halves are reflections, the molecule proves superimposable on its own mirror image despite having two chirality centers, the situation that defines a meso compound.
authoredInteractions:
- Click for selecting an HO, H, or CO2H group on one stereocenter; the reflected counterpart on the other stereocenter highlights across the plane, clarifying why the two halves cancel molecular handedness.
- Toggle between structure-only, model-only, and overlay views of the symmetry plane; the pale plane persists across representations, showing that the same internal reflection explains achirality despite two chirality centers.
authoredContext:
The 2R,3S and 2S,3R structures are identical because the molecule has a plane of symmetry and is therefore achiral. The symmetry plane cuts through the C2–C3 bond, making one half of the molecule a mirror image of the other half (the figure). Because of the plane of symmetry, the molecule is achiral, despite the fact that it has two chirality centers. Such compounds, which are achiral, yet contain chirality centers, are called meso compounds (me-zo). Thus, tartaric acid exists in three stereoisomeric forms: two enantiomers and one meso form.

A symmetry plane through the C2–C3 bond of meso-tartaric acid makes the molecule achiral.

The wedge-dash structure and ball-and-stick model of tartaric acid. C2 and C3 have a horizontal symmetry plane.

Some physical properties of the three stereoisomers are listed in the table. The (+)- and (−)-tartaric acids have identical melting points, solubilities, and densities, but they differ in the sign of their rotation of plane-polarized light. The meso isomer, by contrast, is diastereomeric with the (+) and (−) forms. It has no mirror-image relationship to (+)- and (−)-tartaric acids, is a different compound altogether, and thus has different physical properties.

demo_steps.title: Start with the structural drawing
demo_steps.narration: The two C centers are stacked vertically, and the pale blue sheet cuts horizontally between them. Clicking HO, H, or CO2H on one carbon should highlight the matching reflected group on the other carbon.

demo_steps.title: Switch to the molecular model

demo_steps.title: Compare both representations

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a front-facing, slightly three-quarter perspective similar to the source. Overall composition should fit in a wide frame about 7.0 world units wide by 3.4 high. In Structure only mode center the flat drawing at x=0; in Model only mode center the ball-and-stick model at x=0; in Structure + model mode place the structural drawing on the left centered near x=-2.2 and the molecular model on the right centered near x=2.2. The structural drawing is essentially a 2D XY drawing at z=0: upper C at (0, 0.75, 0), lower C at (0, -0.75, 0), vertical C-C bond from y=0.48 to y=-0.48. Upper H label at (0, 1.42, 0) in blue #0076b6 with a dashed bond from upper C upward. Lower H label at (0, -1.42, 0) with a dashed bond downward. Upper HO label at (-0.78, 0.95, 0) in magenta #ff00a8 with a bold wedge slanting down-left to up-right between C and HO. Lower HO label at (-0.78, -0.95, 0) mirrored vertically with a bold wedge slanting up-left to down-right. Upper CO2H label at (0.92, 0.96, 0) in green #00815a with a solid slanted bond from upper C to the right. Lower CO2H label at (0.92, -0.96, 0) mirrored vertically. Draw label text CO₂H with subscript 2 if supported. Symmetry plane in the structural panel: translucent pale cyan #bfefff at about 45 percent opacity, a thin parallelogram centered at (0, 0, -0.03), width about 1.5, depth about 0.42, visually horizontal with its receding edges angled down-left/up-right like the source. Place black 'Symmetry plane' text to the right of the plane, around (1.3, -0.05, 0). Ball-and-stick model: central gray carbon spheres radius 0.18-0.22, color #59666c, at (0, 0.62, 0) and (0, -0.62, 0), connected by a light gray cylinder radius 0.055. The molecular symmetry plane is a larger translucent pale cyan parallelogram centered at y=0, spanning x about -1.55 to +1.75 and z about -0.35 to +0.35, very thin, with its front edge horizontal and receding diagonal matching the source. Upper half: from upper C, red oxygen group extends upper-left: first red sphere #b73a2f radius 0.16 at (-0.62, 0.92, 0.02), second red sphere radius 0.12 at (-0.75, 1.48, 0.00), connected by gray cylinders. Upper blue H sphere radius 0.11 at (0.18, 0.18, 0.18), connected to upper C and partially visible near the central bond. Upper green CO2H group extends to the right: main green sphere #25b96b radius 0.20 at (0.72, 0.98, 0.05), branch green sphere radius 0.18 at (0.72, 1.62, 0.00), small terminal green sphere radius 0.12 at (1.05, 1.87, 0.02), right terminal green sphere radius 0.17 at (1.25, 0.86, 0.06). Lower half is the mirror across y=0: red spheres at (-0.62, -0.92, 0.02) and (-0.75, -1.48, 0.00); blue H at (0.18, -0.18, 0.18); green spheres at (0.72, -0.98, 0.05), (0.72, -1.62, 0.00), (1.05, -1.87, 0.02), and (1.25, -0.86, 0.06). The upper and lower HO/H/CO2H sets must be equal-size mirror partners, not progressively scaled by vertical position. Click targets: upper HO group includes its red/HO label and wedge or red oxygen cluster; upper H includes blue H label/sphere and dashed bond; upper CO2H includes green label/green cluster and bond. Mirrored counterparts are the corresponding lower groups. Highlight selected and reflected counterpart using yellow #ffd42a outline/glow while leaving the plane cyan.
interactionPlan.notes: Render structural drawing labels as crisp CSS2D or signed-distance-field text so HO, H, C, CO₂H, and Symmetry plane remain readable. Wedge bonds in the structural drawing can be triangular meshes; dashed bonds can be short black line segments. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial or MeshStandardMaterial for shaded spheres in the model, with small specular highlights. For the representation toggle, keep both scene groups loaded and animate opacity/position rather than rebuilding. In Structure + model mode preserve the original side-by-side relationship. The cyan plane should remain visible in every mode and should not be occluded completely by atoms; use transparent material with depthWrite=false if needed. Click highlighting should work symmetrically from either stereocenter: clicking an upper group highlights its lower mirror partner, and clicking a lower group highlights its upper mirror partner.

demo_steps.narration: The CO2H groups on the right are also related by reflection through the plane. Matching all substituent types confirms that one half of the molecule mirrors the other.

demo_steps.title: Meso conclusion
demo_steps.narration: All three substituent pairs match across the plane. Because the molecule contains an internal symmetry plane, it is superimposable on its mirror image and is meso rather than optically active.

plan.geometry_notes: Overall layout: use a wide frame about 7.2 world units wide by 3.4 high. Default view MUST show both panels simultaneously, with no representation toggle. Place the structural drawing on the left centered at x=-2.25, y=0, z=0, scaled to about 2.15 units tall and 1.9 units wide. Place the ball-and-stick model on the right centered at x=2.15, y=0, z=0, about 2.7 units tall and 2.4 units wide. Leave about 0.7 world units of empty space between the structural formula and molecular model so they read as paired but separate depictions. Color palette: black bonds/text #111111, structural H blue #0076b6, structural HO magenta #d61aa0, structural CO2H green #15894f, central carbon dark gray #4f5b5f, model bonds light gray #b8b8b8, oxygen red #c33a2f, hydrogen blue #2d8fd7, carboxyl-group green #22a86b, symmetry plane pale cyan #bdefff with opacity 0.38 to 0.48, selection halo yellow #ffd54a with low opacity. Structural drawing coordinates are local to the left panel before applying the x=-2.25 offset: upper C text at (0, 0.58, 0), lower C text at (0, -0.58, 0), vertical C-C bond from (0, 0.42, 0) to (0, -0.42, 0). Upper H at (0, 1.18, 0) with a dashed vertical bond from (0, 0.72, 0) to (0, 1.02, 0). Lower H at (0, -1.18, 0) with a dashed vertical bond from (0, -0.72, 0) to (0, -1.02, 0). Upper HO label at (-0.73, 0.82, 0), connected to upper C by a filled triangular wedge whose narrow point touches the C and whose wide end points upper-left. Lower HO label at (-0.73, -0.82, 0), connected by the vertically mirrored wedge. Upper CO2H label at (0.88, 0.82, 0), connected by a simple solid slanted bond from the upper C toward upper-right. Lower CO2H label at (0.88, -0.82, 0), connected by the vertically mirrored solid slanted bond. Use CO₂H with subscript 2 if possible. Structural symmetry plane: draw a thin translucent parallelogram centered at local (0, 0, -0.025), long horizontal dimension about 1.65 units, apparent thickness/depth about 0.38 units, with the left and right edges slanting slightly down-left/up-right so it reads like the pale blue edge-on plane in the source. Put the label 'Symmetry plane' in black at local (1.25, -0.06, 0.02), aligned horizontally. Molecular model coordinates are local to the right panel before applying the x=2.15 offset. Use +Y as vertical screen direction; the mirror plane is the horizontal XZ plane at y=0. Set upper central carbon at (0, 0.62, 0), lower central carbon at (0, -0.62, 0), radius 0.19, joined by a cylinder radius 0.055. Use genuinely tetrahedral-looking substituent directions: the C-C bond from the upper carbon points downward toward the lower carbon, while the three upper substituent bonds point generally upward with separated x/z depth components; the lower half is the exact reflection across y=0, so x and z coordinates are identical and y coordinates change sign. Upper H sphere radius 0.105 at (0.05, 0.86, -0.62), connected to upper carbon; lower H at (0.05, -0.86, -0.62). Upper HO first red oxygen radius 0.16 at (-0.58, 0.86, 0.38), connected to upper carbon; upper second small red sphere radius 0.105 at (-0.82, 1.20, 0.62), connected to the first red oxygen. Lower HO first red oxygen at (-0.58, -0.86, 0.38), lower second red sphere at (-0.82, -1.20, 0.62). Upper CO2H main green sphere radius 0.18 at (0.62, 0.86, 0.12), connected to upper carbon; upper branch green sphere radius 0.155 at (0.82, 1.30, -0.18), upper small terminal green sphere radius 0.105 at (1.08, 1.54, -0.35), and upper right terminal green sphere radius 0.14 at (1.13, 0.83, 0.22). Lower CO2H main green sphere at (0.62, -0.86, 0.12), lower branch green sphere at (0.82, -1.30, -0.18), lower small terminal green sphere at (1.08, -1.54, -0.35), and lower right terminal green sphere at (1.13, -0.83, 0.22). Add cylinders between each bonded pair. Molecular symmetry plane: translucent pale cyan rectangle/parallelogram lying exactly in y=0, centered near local (0.18, 0, 0), spanning x from about -1.25 to +1.45 and z from -0.58 to +0.72; orient it so the front edge appears nearly horizontal and the receding edges show slight perspective. It must pass between, not through, the two central carbon spheres. Equal substituent types must have equal sizes in the upper and lower halves. Selection halos: hidden when guidedFocus='none' and when no click target is selected. When active, use thin low-opacity yellow outline rings or small glow shells around only the selected group and its mirror partner; do not show large default yellow rings and do not obscure the cyan plane.
plan.notes: Render the scene as a simultaneous comparison, not as separate panels hidden behind a representation toggle. Keep the structural drawing fixed in screen-facing orientation on the left while allowing orbit interaction to rotate only the right molecular-model group or a right-side orbit container; the left drawing should not spin away from the reader. Use CSS2D or signed-distance-field text for crisp C, H, HO, CO₂H, and Symmetry plane labels. Use triangular meshes for wedge bonds and segmented line geometry for dashed bonds. For the molecule, use MeshStandardMaterial with clear directional lighting and ambient fill; enable depth testing so front and back substituents occlude correctly. Use transparent material for cyan planes with depthWrite=false and renderOrder after opaque atoms so the plane remains visible without hiding the model. Click targets should be group-level: H, HO, and CO2H on either the structural drawing or the molecule; clicking an upper group highlights the lower mirror partner and clicking a lower group highlights the upper mirror partner. The guidedFocus state should drive the same subtle highlight system used by clicks, with 'none' showing no halos.
